groups.start-simple: Native Python, SQL and Power BI

features.title: Python and Spark SQL, together
features.description: Use Python and Spark SQL together to load files and create Lakehouse tables. Weaver runs the steps in the right order.

features.title: Ordinary T-SQL
features.description: Keep ordinary SELECTs, without a proprietary modelling language or macros.

features.title: Keep using Power BI files
features.description: Apply modelling standards, run unit tests and deploy Reports using standard Power BI project files (PBIP and TMDL).

features.title: Work in Fabric or your own editor
features.description: Write code in VS Code or another editor on Windows, macOS or Linux, or work entirely in Fabric Notebooks. Deploy native Power BI models and Reports without Power BI Desktop.

features.title: Built for developers and AI agents
features.description: Use readable terminal output or structured JSON results from Check, Build, Load, Test and Health. The guide shows how to give an agent a development workspace, preview changes and run without prompts.

features.title: Query your Fabric data from the terminal
features.description: Use weaver execute to inspect a Warehouse, Lakehouse or model with T-SQL, Spark SQL, Python or DAX. Read the results without switching tools. Submitted SQL and Python can also change data.

features.title: Pick up where each table left off
features.description: You supply inserts, updates and explicit deletes. Weaver applies them and tracks each table or folder's progress separately, even when several read the same source.

features.title: Test data and calculations
features.description: Compare actual and expected results or find invalid rows using Python, SQL and DAX.

features.title: Data-quality safeguards
features.description: Keep rejected rows and stop unusually large proposed updates or deletes before they reach your tables.

features.title: Run a table, a branch or an item
features.description: Preview the work you intend to run. Select an item for its ordered loads, or name an object and explicitly include the upstream or downstream work you need.

features.title: Keep a failed step from stopping unrelated work
features.description: Choose fault-tolerant loading to let independent branches continue after a failure. Completed changes remain in place; inspect the failed step before retrying it.

features.title: Catch up after a source changes
features.description: Use load --stale to rerun loads that need attention, then test --stale for validations that are no longer current. You can recover the affected work without repeating the whole project.

features.title: Organisation-wide modelling standards
features.description: Apply shared native TMDL policy across Semantic Models instead of repeating formats and conventions.

features.title: Built-in modelling rules
features.description: Automatically hide foreign keys and create measure selectors using standard TMDL annotations.

features.title: Write your own modelling rules in Python
features.description: Add your own Python rules when you need more than Weaver's built-in modelling options.

features.title: Reuse models without copying them
features.description: Start from a shared model and create versions for different audiences without maintaining complete copies.

features.title: Unit testing for Semantic Models
features.description: Unit test DAX measures against independent expected results, including SQL calculations over managed Lakehouse or Warehouse sources.

features.title: Connect Reports to the right models
features.description: Deploy the same Report to different workspaces. Weaver checks that it connects to the intended Power BI model.

features.title: See all your work in one place
features.description: Weaver keeps its Catalogue of deployed items, dependencies and run results in an ordinary Fabric Warehouse. There's no separate monitoring service to run.

features.title: See what is up to date or needs attention
features.description: See what is up to date, waiting, failed or inconsistent across your managed Fabric work.

features.title: See run history and results
features.description: See what ran, how long it took, row counts, data changes and recorded results.

features.title: Several teams on one Dashboard
features.description: One Dashboard can read several teams' catalogues, show which workspaces supply which, and narrow every page by workspace, item and object in the Filters pane.

features.title: Static pages for sharing
features.description: Export a snapshot of the deployed model's data as HTML, from the CLI or a notebook. A downloaded local copy opens without a running Fabric capacity.

features.title: Update only what changed
features.description: Update changed source definitions and the work that depends on them, while leaving unchanged parts in place.

features.title: See changes before applying them
features.description: Preview what will change, where it will go and whether anything will be replaced or deleted.

features.title: Review deployments before applying them
features.description: Prepare a fixed deployment plan, review it and apply it later without changing the plan.

features.title: Protect important data
features.description: Keep irreplaceable sources outside managed targets and use Build replacement guards for protected owned objects.

features.title: Connect the work without merging the projects
features.description: Supply the catalogues for the teams involved. Health follows their recorded dependencies; Load and Test coordinate the work you select and write each result to its owning catalogue.

features.title: Run independent branches together
features.description: Set concurrency limits for the run and its resources. Weaver can overlap independent Spark and Warehouse work while keeping dependent steps in order.

features.title: Coordinate the hand-off between engines
features.description: When your Warehouse reads a loaded Lakehouse table, Weaver waits for its SQL endpoint refresh. A shortcut reading another team's Warehouse table also waits for the source's OneLake publication.

features.title: When teams read each other's results
features.description: If teams read each other's results, Weaver reports the cycle and runs selected objects once in a consistent order. A reader closing the loop uses the producer's available result from an earlier run.
